standard.title: Method for Estimation of Total Dietary Fibre in Foodstuffs (पहला पुनरीक्षण) (First Revision)
standard.sector: Food and Agriculture / Test Methods for Food Products

sectional_committee.name: Test Methods for Food Products Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies an enzymatic and gravimetric method for the determination of insoluble, soluble, and total dietary fibre after the enzymatic digestion of carbohydrate, protein, and starch in foodstuffs.
standard.scope: This standard specifies an enzymatic and gravimetric method for the determination of insoluble, soluble, and total dietary fibre after the enzymatic digestion of carbohydrate, protein, and starch in foodstuffs.

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this reaffirmed copy (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 11062 : 2019 is a laboratory testing methodology rather than a direct physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its sampling, milling, lipid extraction, and enzymatic-gravimetric calculation protocols is strictly mandated in public sector food quality testing, commercial nutritional labeling (FSSAI audits), agricultural university research, and national crop-procurement specifications across India to certify dietary fibre content and support food labeling claims.
requirements: Defines dietary fibre as the sum of polysaccharides and lignin present in human diets that are not digested by the endogenous secretions of the upper gastro-intestinal tract (including gums, mucilages, and associated plant cell wall components resistant to alimentary enzymes).
Classifies dietary fibre based on water solubility into Insoluble Dietary Fibre (IDF) (less fermentable fibre) and Soluble Dietary Fibre (SDF) (fermentable fibre).
Establishes the enzymatic and gravimetric method (AOAC-based) as the standard, mimicking the human digestive process to resolve insoluble, soluble, and total dietary fibre.
Mandates that each food sample must be analyzed in duplicate, along with a parallel reagent blank to correct for protein from enzymes and ash from buffers.

Requires drawing a representative sample of the entire lot. Grains must be milled to a precise particle size of 0.5 - 1 mm in a cyclone mill. The dry matter content must be determined after drying for 5 hours at 105°C.

Mandates lipid extraction prior to enzymatic assay for foodstuffs containing more than 5 percent of lipids. This step facilitates the subsequent removal of free sugars by ethyl alcohol extraction. The lipids must be extracted via 5 hours of Soxhlet extraction using a chloroform-methanol mixture or solvent ether.

Defines the calculation of Total Dietary Fibre (TDF) as the sum of insoluble and soluble fractions:
TDF (Percent) = IDF (Percent) + SDF (Percent)
Requires expressing the final results as g/100 g on a dry mass basis (or 'as is' basis as required) after correcting mathematically for moisture and lipid content.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing moisture, lipid weight, or fibre percentage must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be identical to the specified value in the standard.
